newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on soy drop, improved rating.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on soy drop, improved rating.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a drop in most soybean contracts and on indications of improving conditions in U.S. winter wheat, traders said.
USDA Monday said the U.S. winter wheat crop as of Sunday was 60 percent good to excellent, above the 55 percent in that category the previous week.
Wheat held firm in early dealings on a slowdown in wheat harvesting and on concern about dry weather in the U.S. spring wheat growing region.

Rainy weather has slowed early combining of the U.S. hard red winter wheat crop, especially in Oklahoma and cash dealers early Tuesday said rains delayed harvest in Texas. Also, it was raining Tuesday morning in Oklahoma.
Wheat also was underpinned by mounting concerns about dry weather in North Dakota's spring wheat growing region, traders said.
USDA Monday said the U.S. spring wheat crop as of Sunday was 69 percent good to excellent, below the 72 percent in that category the previous week.
Wheat closed 4-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 cents higher, with July down 4-1/2 at $3.63.
